To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Milky Way is a disk-dominated galaxy with a significant thick disk, an oblate halo with an axis ratio of 1:1.6, and a number density of stars in its halo that is 0.5% that of the disk at the solar radius.

(1) the Galaxy consists of an oblate spheroidal halo, thin and thick disks, with a Virgo overdensity and two other overdensities, and (2) no evidence is found for a significant amount of unresolved clumpy substructures at scales ranging from 50 pc in the solar neighborhood to 2 kpc in halo.

the stellar number density distribution of the Galaxy is consistent with an oblate halo with a power-law density profile, a thick and thin disk component, and that the data are consistent with the hypothesis that the Galaxy is composed of these components alone.

the Milky Way has a smooth, well-defined structure with a large-scale disk-halo transition occurring at R ~ 20 kpc.

a smooth, two-exponential model provides an excellent description of the Galactic stellar distribution.
